scope: phase_B_findings_recheck; supplied full current source/tests and explicitly labeled integration diff if present

findings.title: settle() does not bind the settlement owner/operation to the member grant scope before relaxing an unknown
findings.issue: settle() validates only the operation row and window ledger; a caller holding the owner can call settle(owner, ref, outcome='unknown', actual=0) on a fence that was never actually invoked (e.g. the no-HTTP compound preparation case), releasing the conservative reserved/unknown charge to zero without any provider evidence. The fence (state='unknown') does persist, so the operation cannot be replayed, matching the documented conservative-but-reconcilable contract, so this is not an allow or retry defect.
findings.fix: Document that actual settlement is governed by the reconciliation path and must be bound to provider evidence, or add an explicit reconciliation receipt requirement. No fail-open behavior was found.

findings.summary: All three prior P1 allegations are resolved in the current code: replace_grant now requires an unrevoked target row (policy.py:160-164) so a revoked grant identity cannot be revived at a higher revision and reauthorization needs a new grant_id, verified by test_revoke_then_replace_cannot_restore_the_same_grant_identity; saved confirmations are checksum-verified on load with exact proposal/owner/version/digest/time/expiry binding and clamp (actions.py:55-79), missing or changed checksums fail closed with a new-preview instruction rather than repairing an approval, and one-use consumption is enforced via consumed=true plus the attempt fence; compound no-HTTP preparation is deliberately non-replayable and the concrete counterexample (test_compound_no_http_reconciles_actual_zero_without_clearing_fence) shows actual=0 settlement releases the conservative charge while preserving the unknown fence, so the #35 claim of irrecoverable cost or allowed I/O is not supported. No P0 or P1 executable defects remain; the single P2 note is informational about the trust model of settle() and does not alter fail-closed or one-use guarantees.
